compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
In the fictional project below, both colleagues have the same footage, data, budget and deadline. They can propose the same changes and have the same opportunity to confer or reflect privately.

Each row illustrates one preference. Either colleague can use either approach. The examples cannot identify a type.

| Shared situation | ESFP: possible emphasis | INFJ: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both review the same decline in views | The recorded dates, segments and retention figures that differ from earlier episodes | A pattern connecting the same changes across several episodes | S/N: concrete details or patterns across observations |
| Both read the same set of viewer comments | The specific clips and timestamps viewers mention | An emerging theme across the same comments, to check against other evidence | S/N: individual observations or possible connections |
| Both consider how to describe a possible relaunch | Work through the same idea by discussing it with colleagues | Work through the same idea by reflecting privately | E/I: outward engagement or inward reflection |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Imagine two colleagues reviewing a show with declining views. Both may want to preserve what the audience values. That concern can fit the shared Feeling preference and can also reflect the job.

Feeling describes what carries weight in a judgment. It cannot establish who is more affected by criticism or how much someone cares about the work.

The three differences concern separate questions about attention, information and outward arrangements.

E/I concerns where attention and energy go. Someone can discuss a concern with others or think about it privately. Neither approach specifies what information they will use.

S/N concerns what stands out when taking in information. A colleague might focus on a recorded detail in one episode or a pattern connecting several episodes. Either person can consider both.

J/P concerns how much to settle or keep open in the outside world. A person can agree to a firm deadline and still keep several format options open.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: deciding whether to change the same show

In a fictional production team, views have dropped thirty per cent over three months. Both colleagues have the same ten episodes, audience data, budget and authority to propose a change.

One line of inquiry is to look at which segments lost viewers and what comments referred to those moments. Another is to look for a theme across episodes that might explain a change in what viewers want. Both can use the same evidence and ask both questions.

One unusual episode can distort the first comparison. A plausible pattern can also turn out to reflect a few isolated comments. A small test can help the team see whether a proposed change is worth exploring, but its result needs to be weighed with the rest of the evidence.

The dominant and inferior labels describe positions in the model. They do not tell you who will notice a detail, consider a long-term outcome or feel comfortable in a busy setting.

The Myers & Briggs Foundation lists Thinking (Te or Ti) as the tertiary function for both types. This article uses Te for ESFP and Ti for INFJ. comparison.summary:
ESFP and INFJ share Feeling (F). They differ on Extraversion and Introversion (E/I), Sensing and Intuition (S/N), and Judging and Perceiving (J/P). In Myers-Briggs type dynamics, ESFP leads with extraverted Sensing (Se) and INFJ leads with introverted Intuition (Ni).

- **Shared F.** Feeling describes a preference for weighing values and effects on people when making a decision. It does not measure sensitivity or tell you how someone recovers after a difficult day.
- **E/I.** ESFP’s E describes a preference for directing attention and energy outward. INFJ’s I describes a preference for directing them inward. Either person can speak at length or want time alone.
- **S/N.** ESFP’s S emphasises concrete details and experience. INFJ’s N emphasises patterns, connections and possibilities. Both can use the same observations.
- **J/P.** INFJ’s J describes a preference for structure and closure in the outside world. ESFP’s P describes a preference for openness to new information and options. Either person can make a plan and revise it.

Under the convention used here, ESFP is Se–Fi–Te–Ni and INFJ is Ni–Fe–Ti–Se. Se and Ni switch the dominant and inferior positions. That swap holds regardless of how the tertiary Thinking function is marked.

Either person can review the analytics or question a show’s direction. Their responsibility, experience and deadline can explain what they do first. A single decision cannot identify a type.

compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
In the fictional project below, both colleagues have the same footage, data, budget and deadline. They can propose the same changes and have the same opportunity to confer or reflect privately.

Each row illustrates one preference. Either colleague can use either approach. The examples cannot identify a type.

| Shared situation | ESFP: possible emphasis | INFJ: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both review the same decline in views | The recorded dates, segments and retention figures that differ from earlier episodes | A pattern connecting the same changes across several episodes | S/N: concrete details or patterns across observations |
| Both read the same set of viewer comments | The specific clips and timestamps viewers mention | An emerging theme across the same comments, to check against other evidence | S/N: individual observations or possible connections |
| Both consider how to describe a possible relaunch | Work through the same idea by discussing it with colleagues | Work through the same idea by reflecting privately | E/I: outward engagement or inward reflection |
| Both review how to proceed after a trial episode | Keep multiple permissible options open until the agreed decision point | Set a provisional next step under the same criteria and decision point | J/P: keeping options available or giving the plan more structure |
| Both must meet the same platform specifications | Keep more than one compliant version available until review | Choose a provisional compliant version for the same review | J/P: flexibility or provisional closure within the same constraints |
| Both review the same season three months later | The episodes that viewers returned to and the parts with the longest retention | The pattern across those figures and what it may suggest about the season’s direction | S/N: concrete records or a possible pattern |

A colleague with editing experience may know where to find the most useful metric. Someone asked to lead the review may be the first to speak. Neither action by itself tells you about type.
compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Imagine two colleagues reviewing a show with declining views. Both may want to preserve what the audience values. That concern can fit the shared Feeling preference and can also reflect the job.

Feeling describes what carries weight in a judgment. It cannot establish who is more affected by criticism or how much someone cares about the work.

The three differences concern separate questions about attention, information and outward arrangements.

E/I concerns where attention and energy go. Someone can discuss a concern with others or think about it privately. Neither approach specifies what information they will use.

S/N concerns what stands out when taking in information. A colleague might focus on a recorded detail in one episode or a pattern connecting several episodes. Either person can consider both.

J/P concerns how much to settle or keep open in the outside world. A person can agree to a firm deadline and still keep several format options open.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: deciding whether to change the same show

In a fictional production team, views have dropped thirty per cent over three months. Both colleagues have the same ten episodes, audience data, budget and authority to propose a change.

One line of inquiry is to look at which segments lost viewers and what comments referred to those moments. Another is to look for a theme across episodes that might explain a change in what viewers want. Both can use the same evidence and ask both questions.

One unusual episode can distort the first comparison. A plausible pattern can also turn out to reflect a few isolated comments. A small test can help the team see whether a proposed change is worth exploring, but its result needs to be weighed with the rest of the evidence.

Either colleague can check a retention figure or suggest an explanation. The order depends in part on which questions the team has already answered.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: why Se and Ni switch positions

For ESFP, P points to an outward-facing perceiving function. S makes that Se, and E makes it dominant. For INFJ, J points to an outward-facing judging function. F makes that Fe, and I makes it auxiliary to the inward-facing dominant function, Ni.

The displayed stacks are Se–Fi–Te–Ni and Ni–Fe–Ti–Se. ESFP has dominant Se and inferior Ni. INFJ has dominant Ni and inferior Se. Their auxiliary Feeling functions differ: introverted Feeling (Fi) for ESFP and extraverted Feeling (Fe) for INFJ.

The dominant and inferior labels describe positions in the model. They do not tell you who will notice a detail, consider a long-term outcome or feel comfortable in a busy setting.

The Myers & Briggs Foundation lists Thinking (Te or Ti) as the tertiary function for both types. This article uses Te for ESFP and Ti for INFJ. Different choices may change which Thinking abbreviation is shared, but they do not change the Se/Ni swap. See the [ESFP profile](/en/personality/esfp) and the [INFJ profile](/en/personality/infj) for their four preferences.

The three fictional scenes below illustrate ways to weigh the same situation. Assign production work by experience, availability and responsibility.

If a colleague wants to test a format and another wants to clarify the purpose, make both questions explicit. A test can tell you something about the format. A discussion can clarify whether the test addresses the right problem.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: when to test a relaunch

In a fictional review, views have fallen for three months. Both colleagues have the same data and agree the show needs attention. One option is to test a new format next week. Another is to review what the show promises viewers before deciding what to change.

A small test may give the team new information quickly. A review of the show’s purpose can expose a question the test would miss. Both colleagues can propose either approach. If they run a small test, changing one feature can make its results easier to interpret.

Ask each colleague to write what they would do if the decline continues and what evidence would change their mind. Compare the notes to see whether the disagreement is about the goal, the proposed change or the means to test it.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: when a friend asks you to keep a story private

In a fictional example, a friend shares a difficult experience and asks two people not to write about it. Both hear the same request and have the same responsibility to respect it.

Either person might see a connection to what they are working on. That observation does not permit the story to be used. It also cannot show whose Feeling preference is stronger.

Keep the experience out of the script. Changing names or details does not override the friend’s request. Discuss any use only if the friend raises it again, and only with their explicit agreement about what can be shared.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: delivering a sample cut in two weeks

In a fictional project, both colleagues have the same two-week deadline and the same length and cover specifications. They can agree on a provisional structure or keep more than one compliant version available for review.

Either can outline the story or make the rough cut. Assign the work based on experience, time and responsibility. The choice of who does what gives no basis for identifying a type.

They share Se and Ni in opposite dominant and inferior positions. ESFP has dominant Se and inferior Ni. INFJ has dominant Ni and inferior Se.

Yes. Following a trend and planning for the long term are both possible for either type.

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
Imagine two colleagues reviewing a show with declining views. Both may want to preserve what the audience values. That concern can fit the shared Feeling preference and can also reflect the job.

Feeling describes what carries weight in a judgment. It cannot establish who is more affected by criticism or how much someone cares about the work.

The three differences concern separate questions about attention, information and outward arrangements.

E/I concerns where attention and energy go. Someone can discuss a concern with others or think about it privately. Neither approach specifies what information they will use.

S/N concerns what stands out when taking in information. A colleague might focus on a recorded detail in one episode or a pattern connecting several episodes. Either person can consider both.

J/P concerns how much to settle or keep open in the outside world. A person can agree to a firm deadline and still keep several format options open.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: deciding whether to change the same show

In a fictional production team, views have dropped thirty per cent over three months. Both colleagues have the same ten episodes, audience data, budget and authority to propose a change.

One line of inquiry is to look at which segments lost viewers and what comments referred to those moments. Another is to look for a theme across episodes that might explain a change in what viewers want. Both can use the same evidence and ask both questions.

One unusual episode can distort the first comparison. A plausible pattern can also turn out to reflect a few isolated comments. A small test can help the team see whether a proposed change is worth exploring, but its result needs to be weighed with the rest of the evidence.

Either colleague can check a retention figure or suggest an explanation. The order depends in part on which questions the team has already answered.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: why Se and Ni switch positions

For ESFP, P points to an outward-facing perceiving function. S makes that Se, and E makes it dominant. For INFJ, J points to an outward-facing judging function. F makes that Fe, and I makes it auxiliary to the inward-facing dominant function, Ni.

The displayed stacks are Se–Fi–Te–Ni and Ni–Fe–Ti–Se. ESFP has dominant Se and inferior Ni. INFJ has dominant Ni and inferior Se. Their auxiliary Feeling functions differ: introverted Feeling (Fi) for ESFP and extraverted Feeling (Fe) for INFJ.

The dominant and inferior labels describe positions in the model. They do not tell you who will notice a detail, consider a long-term outcome or feel comfortable in a busy setting.

The Myers & Briggs Foundation lists Thinking (Te or Ti) as the tertiary function for both types. This article uses Te for ESFP and Ti for INFJ. Different choices may change which Thinking abbreviation is shared, but they do not change the Se/Ni swap. See the [ESFP profile](/en/personality/esfp) and the [INFJ profile](/en/personality/infj) for their four preferences.

In the fictional project below, both colleagues have the same footage, data, budget and deadline. They can propose the same changes and have the same opportunity to confer or reflect privately.

Each row illustrates one preference. Either colleague can use either approach. The examples cannot identify a type.

| Shared situation | ESFP: possible emphasis | INFJ: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both review the same decline in views | The recorded dates, segments and retention figures that differ from earlier episodes | A pattern connecting the same changes across several episodes | S/N: concrete details or patterns across observations |
| Both read the same set of viewer comments | The specific clips and timestamps viewers mention | An emerging theme across the same comments, to check against other evidence | S/N: individual observations or possible connections |
| Both consider how to describe a possible relaunch | Work through the same idea by discussing it with colleagues | Work through the same idea by reflecting privately | E/I: outward engagement or inward reflection |
| Both review how to proceed after a trial episode | Keep multiple permissible options open until the agreed decision point | Set a provisional next step under the same criteria and decision point | J/P: keeping options available or giving the plan more structure |
| Both must meet the same platform specifications | Keep more than one compliant version available until review | Choose a provisional compliant version for the same review | J/P: flexibility or provisional closure within the same constraints |
| Both review the same season three months later | The episodes that viewers returned to and the parts with the longest retention | The pattern across those figures and what it may suggest about the season’s direction | S/N: concrete records or a possible pattern |

A colleague with editing experience may know where to find the most useful metric. Someone asked to lead the review may be the first to speak. Neither action by itself tells you about type.

The three fictional scenes below illustrate ways to weigh the same situation. Assign production work by experience, availability and responsibility.

If a colleague wants to test a format and another wants to clarify the purpose, make both questions explicit. A test can tell you something about the format. A discussion can clarify whether the test addresses the right problem.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: when to test a relaunch

In a fictional review, views have fallen for three months. Both colleagues have the same data and agree the show needs attention. One option is to test a new format next week. Another is to review what the show promises viewers before deciding what to change.

A small test may give the team new information quickly. A review of the show’s purpose can expose a question the test would miss. Both colleagues can propose either approach. If they run a small test, changing one feature can make its results easier to interpret.

Ask each colleague to write what they would do if the decline continues and what evidence would change their mind. Compare the notes to see whether the disagreement is about the goal, the proposed change or the means to test it.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: when a friend asks you to keep a story private

In a fictional example, a friend shares a difficult experience and asks two people not to write about it. Both hear the same request and have the same responsibility to respect it.

Either person might see a connection to what they are working on. That observation does not permit the story to be used. It also cannot show whose Feeling preference is stronger.

Keep the experience out of the script. Changing names or details does not override the friend’s request. Discuss any use only if the friend raises it again, and only with their explicit agreement about what can be shared.

### ### ESFP and INFJ: delivering a sample cut in two weeks

In a fictional project, both colleagues have the same two-week deadline and the same length and cover specifications. They can agree on a provisional structure or keep more than one compliant version available for review.

Either can outline the story or make the rough cut. Assign the work based on experience, time and responsibility. The choice of who does what gives no basis for identifying a type.

Someone may be more affected by criticism when a project is demanding or when they have invested heavily in it. Shared Feeling gives no basis for inferring how someone will react or recover.

Both types can plan ahead and revise a plan. J/P concerns structure and openness in the outside world. It does not measure how effectively someone executes a plan.

Writing, editing and production scheduling are skills. Compare people’s experience with what the task requires when assigning work.

items.question: ### What is the main difference between ESFP and INFJ?

items.answer:
They share Se and Ni in opposite dominant and inferior positions. ESFP has dominant Se and inferior Ni. INFJ has dominant Ni and inferior Se.

Their auxiliary functions are Fi and Fe, respectively. Their tertiary function is Thinking, written Te for ESFP and Ti for INFJ in this article. The Foundation also allows the other orientation for each. A function position cannot establish a person’s abilities or predict a single reaction.
items.question: ### Which cognitive functions do ESFP and INFJ share?

items.answer:
Yes. Following a trend and planning for the long term are both possible for either type.

When reflecting on S/N, consider what information stood out in several comparable situations. Either person can draw on a specific experience and consider how it fits into a broader pattern.
